architecture.design: One first-party generic conversion operation parameterizes source representation, exact target dtype, optional preferred dtype, policy mode, weakness, shape metadata and execution context. A hard target and soft hint have distinct types/branches. Leto supplies shape/layout and custom interchange protocols; Mnemosyne owns buffers; Melinoe access proof; Themis placement; Hephaestus actual device conversion. Coeus composes tensor/AD/resource semantics. No foreign runtime, Python registry architecture, dynamic hot-path dispatch, implicit widening or CPU fallback is prescribed.

clauses.contract: The public v2 wrapper supports API dispatch and delegates to convert_to_tensor_v2; the ordered registry phases below describe the selected native wrapper path. Custom dispatch can replace that path and is not assumed equivalent.
remaining_obligations: Public dispatch resolution and all custom Composite/Ragged/Sparse implementations remain unclosed.

clauses.contract: Normalize non-None dtype, then non-None dtype_hint via as_dtype, before hook lookup. A valid explicit dtype suppresses the soft conversion attempt, but does not suppress parsing an invalid hint. Exact as_dtype failure taxonomy remains transitive source work.

If __tf_tensor__ is non-None, call it with normalized dtype and name and return its result directly. dtype_hint is not passed. This branch precedes the registry and does not execute the registry return validation. Hook lookup/body exceptions propagate; do not invent registry postvalidation for this branch.

Registry selection matches subclasses and sorts priority, preserving registration order at equal priority. The internal priority0 tuple and public exclusion tuple are exactly (int, float, np.generic, np.ndarray), including subclasses: bool is excluded through int; Python complex is not excluded by that tuple, while NumPy complex scalar types fall under np.generic. List/tuple default conversion uses priority100 and object fallback priority200. With no additional matching registration, Python complex reaches the object fallback; public complex registration with a valid callable is permitted by these checks. Tuple-of-types registration rejects if any member is an excluded subclass. Actual import-time registration and thread/context state are separate obligations.

Only when dtype is None and a hint is supplied, try that converter with the hint. Catch TypeError/ValueError and retry this converter with dtype=None. A normal hinted return of None instead raises AttributeError in the try-else ret.dtype access, outside the TypeError/ValueError handler, before any retry. An unhinted None return fails the later accepted_result_types check with RuntimeError. NotImplemented skips directly to the next converter; it does not cause unhinted retry of the same converter. An incompatible returned dtype raises RuntimeError. Other exceptions propagate.

After NotImplemented handling, a core.Tensor result may call its own __tf_tensor__ with no arguments. Check accepted_result_types (default core.Symbol), then explicit dtype compatibility. Invalid result and incompatible dtype are separate RuntimeErrors. Accepted-result membership is not proof of all Tensor/shape/AD semantics.

For a normal Tensor in the compatible execution context, __tf_tensor__ returns self if dtype is absent/compatible and raises ValueError if incompatible. EagerTensor outside eager execution first requires a graph building_function and then returns graph.capture(self, name=name) without forwarding dtype or invoking the superclass branch; that branch is not an identity or universal mismatch-error promise.
remaining_obligations: Graph capture dtype validation/error order, foreign graph/context, async/distributed tensors and resource/composite return forms remain open.

clauses.contract: Conversion has no shape argument. Native identity preserves the existing logical shape and object. Builtin conversion delegates constant; selected eager NumPy ndarray conversion explicitly copies before EagerTensor construction. Rank-zero, singleton and zero-extent tensors differ. Unknown static TensorShape and runtime tf.shape are distinct; no generic view/stride or host-device zero-copy law follows.

tf.cast parses the destination dtype, may return a matching Tensor/ResourceVariable early, otherwise converts dense/Python x without the destination dtype and then emits Cast if needed. Direct convert_to_tensor(value,dtype=...) is therefore a different conversion sequence. Default Python float construction can round at binary32 before a requested cast to binary64; explicit binary64 construction must be compared separately.
remaining_obligations: Eager native scalar constructor, generated Cast binding, complete dtype/kernel tables and NaN/overflow results are not closed.

clauses.contract: WeakTensor.__tf_tensor__ delegates to its underlying Tensor and convert_to_tensor strips that wrapper. In safe/all mode, patched constant may create weak results when dtype is absent; explicit dtype requests force a strong result. Weakness is a source-level policy axis separate from data dtype, rank and device, and its public construction/binding is not newly admitted here.

Native conversion identity preserves the existing AD value; host-origin construction is not a differentiable link to Python/NumPy memory. Custom conversion may run differentiable operations and requires its own VJP. Conversion itself does not invent casts or zero gradients. The separate registered Cast rule casts cotangents back only for its listed real/complex types and returns None otherwise.
remaining_obligations: Forward/higher/batched AD, custom dispatch, Composite/resource gradients, dtype-specific casts and weak tangent representation remain unresolved.

proposal.no_equivalence_claim: Framework-shaped source contracts remain independent. Similar NumPy/JAX/Torch names, dtype tables or shape formulas are not semantic or implementation equivalence evidence.
proposal.selected_domain: Source-phase obligations for the v2 selected native wrapper; native dense host/CPU examples plus explicit protocol/mode/context branches. No complete admissibility partition or runtime/device/gradient qualification.
proposal.selection_rationale: One existing unmapped public conversion endpoint supplies the missing input boundary for already-partial raw cast/add/shape contracts. This complements JAX/NumPy source policies and pending Torch .10 without another publicness-classification pass or whole promotion-table program.

supporting_distinctions.contract: OFF is initial state. LEGACY enables NumPy-style Tensor operators. SAFE/ALL enable automatic conversion wrappers, and are not the legacy path. The public enable_numpy_behavior source also enables slicing/methods, sets prefer_float32 and warns to configure safe/all at program start; isolate reference processes by mode.

Raw normal tf.add converts x, then y using x dtype only as a hint, and emits same-T Add/AddV2. LEGACY Tensor + operator explicitly promotes before dispatch; it does not prove raw tf.add mixed tensors are promoted. SAFE/ALL wrappers infer dtype/weakness, cast/convert both operands and rewrap. NotImplementedError warns and selects old semantics; TypeError or scalar overflow does not take that fallback. This source fallback is observable and never accelerator execution credit.

The finite flexible table has weak/strong keys. Python bool is strong and tested before int; Python int must fit int32; Python float is weakfloat32 and complex weakcomplex128. Strong int32+float32 is ALL-only, int32+float64 SAFE. These are selected source relations, not a complete public dtype- or kernel-legality table. Unsupported composite types and unavailable joins raise NotImplementedError for callers to handle.

The source-exported experimental NumPy result_type selects flexible inference in SAFE/ALL, otherwise preprocesses/flat-flattens values and delegates companion NumPy result_type with prefer_float32/canonicalization. Its empty-input automatic result is weakfloat32 internally (public result drops weakness). promote_types separately delegates NumPy even in SAFE/ALL; no shared blanket promotion rule. These source-exported names lack records in the selected canonical primary ledger and receive no new identity, admission or mapping.

Keras DTypePolicy has separate variable/compute dtype. mixed_float16 means compute float16, variables float32. convert_input autocasts floating inputs when enabled; integer inputs remain unchanged. Layer.__call__ applies this policy separately. The TensorFlow Keras backend helper deliberately uses conversion then cast for integer/bool targets and casts existing mismatched Tensors, unlike raw tf.convert_to_tensor. No Keras policy widens the raw TF conversion contract.
